labs.title: Labs
labs.lead: Code, build networks, use the terminal, train security and simulate science, all in the browser and without sending anything to any server.
labs.ideLead: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C and C++, PHP, Ruby, Lua, Web and SQL: files, templates, exercises, side console, share link and project download.
labs.redesLead: Build the network, set IPs, VLANs and routes and watch the packet travel.
labs.linuxLead: A shell with a virtual file system and guided exercises.
labs.montadorLead: Build a PC checking every compatibility, use the multimeter, read resistors and solve repair cases for computers, laptops, phones and electronics.
labs.iaLead: Neural networks, nearest neighbours, clustering, overfitting, next-word prediction and bias: models that really train in your browser.
labs.escritorioLead: Documents, spreadsheets and slides (Word, Excel and PowerPoint style), free, in the browser.
labs.escritorioIntro: Three open-source programs from the ArtCraft project, opened right here: write a document, build a spreadsheet with formulas and charts, and prepare a presentation. They open and save .docx, .xlsx and .pptx files.
labs.escritorioLocal: Everything stays in this device's browser: save the file when you finish.
labs.designLead: Posters, posts, invitations and covers from ready-made templates, free and in the browser.
labs.designIntro: The Instituto Lúcia design studio, open to students: pick a template or start from scratch, change texts, photos and colors, and download as PNG, JPG or a print-ready PDF. No account needed: your work stays only in this device's browser. The templates here are generic and carry no Instituto branding, and artwork with the Instituto Lúcia name can't be downloaded: official material is made by the team.
labs.segurancaLead: A training Kali Linux in the browser: a real Linux running isolated, with security tools recreated for learning — all fictitious, plus the defense challenges.
labs.simulacoesLead: Physics, chemistry, biology and maths through PhET's official iframe.
labs.segurancaKaliIntro: This is a training environment, in the spirit of ethical hacking: study attack to learn defense. The desktop mimics Kali Linux and runs a real Linux (isolated, with no network to the real world). The tools — Nmap, Wireshark, Burp, sqlmap and others — are didactic recreations: the output is fictitious and none touches a real system. Attacking a system without written authorization is a crime.
labs.segurancaKaliAviso: On opening, the browser downloads about 8 MB (the emulator and a small Linux image) and boots the system — it takes a few seconds. Best on a computer, with an up-to-date Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
labs.segurancaKaliForaDoAr: The lab is not yet live at the institute's address.
labs.eletricaLead: A real multimeter on the bench, series and parallel, wiring a light and an outlet, the electrician's math and an electronics bench: LED and resistor, capacitor on the oscilloscope, logic gates, power supply and light sensor.
labs.quimicaLead: Acid-base titration with a truly calculated pH curve and four indicators, dilution in a beaker, and the pH scale of household things, with a red-cabbage indicator.
labs.modelosLead: Probability, misleading charts, segregation, cooperation, wealth, epidemics, predator and prey, orbits, waves, cellular automata, regular expressions and your phone as an instrument: predict, run, compare, explain.

portugues: Reading, writing and understanding: from literacy to essay writing.
literatura: From public-domain classics to the literature that comes from the people.
ingles: From zero to reading real texts, without paying for a course.
espanhol: The language of our Latin American neighbours.
chines: Tones, pinyin and the first characters.
russo: Russian from scratch: the Cyrillic alphabet, everyday communication, the case system and reading texts.
artes: Art history, visual arts, theatre, cinema and popular culture.
musica: From sound to the score: theory, reading and practice.
matematica: From times tables to calculus, one step at a time.
fisica: Motion, energy, electricity and the structure of matter.
quimica: From the atom to the reactions behind daily life and industry.
biologia: Life, from the cell to ecosystems, and the health of the people.
astronomia: The sky, the Solar System and the space race.
informatica: From a first contact with the computer to digital security.
programacao: Logic first; then Python and PHP.
inteligencia-artificial: How machines learn, what they can do and whom they serve.
historia: History told from the point of view of those who work.
filosofia: From the Greeks to materialism: learning to think for yourself.
economia: Work, wages, prices, debt and crisis, without the jargon.
politica: State, rights, elections and popular participation.
educacao-popular: Paulo Freire, historical-critical pedagogy and the school as a place where teaching is also learning.
midia: Reading the news critically and making your own media.
meio-ambiente: Climate, land, water and who pays the bill for destruction.
marxismo: Marx and Engels from the start: classes, surplus value and historical materialism.
socialismo: From utopias to revolutions: experiences, achievements and debates.
comunismo: The idea of a classless society and the history of those who fought for it.
ideologia-e-politica: Morality, law, the state and society: how political consciousness is formed, in Brazil, Latin America and the world.
trabalho: Labour rights, trade unions, cooperatives and the solidarity economy.
luta-negra: From resistance to slavery to today's Black movement.
feminismo: Women's struggle for equality, at work and in life.
deficiencia: Rights, accessibility and the struggle against ableism.
povos-indigenas: History, land and resistance of the original peoples.
danca: The body that expresses itself: the social history of dance and the dances of the Brazilian people.
primeiros-socorros: Looking after your health, knowing Brazil's public health system and what to do until help arrives.
educacao-sexual: The body, consent and abuse prevention; health care, STIs, pregnancy and protection methods, with serious information and no taboo.
psicologia: Basic notions and the mental suffering linked to work and social life.
direito: Brazil's 1988 Constitution, workers' rights, the right to strike and to protest.
teologia: History of religions, early Christianity and Liberation Theology.
luta-dos-professores: Strikes, unions and the defence of public schools.
sindicalismo: Workplace organisation, general strikes and collective bargaining.
pessoas-idosas: Pensions, the Statute of Older Persons and the right to grow old with dignity.
favelas: Housing, sanitation, collective building and the organisation of those who built the city.
desenho: From line to perspective: observation, proportion, light and shade, with pencil and paper.
design: Posters, typography and object design: form in the service of those who use it.
teatro: From theatre games to the Theatre of the Oppressed: the stage as a place to think and act.
cinema: How a film is made and read; Brazilian cinema and the cinema of struggle.
edicao-de-video: Cutting, assembling, subtitling and finishing videos for lessons, the newspaper and social media, with free software.
edicao-de-foto: Retouch, crop, color-correct and compose images for posters, the newspaper and social media, from the phone to professional software.
modelagem-3d: Create objects, characters and scenes in three dimensions with free software such as Blender, from the first shape to animation and 3D printing.
educacao-fisica: Body, play, sport and health: movement as a right, not a commodity.
defesa-pessoal: Preventing, getting out of danger and protecting each other: simple techniques, capoeira and other people's fighting arts.
alfabetizacao: Learning to read and write at any age, starting from the words of the learner's own life.
enem: How Brazil's national secondary-school exam works, how to study each area and how to write the essay.
manutencao: Circuits, components, soldering and board repair, plus building and repairing desktops and laptops.
capitalismo: Commodity, wage, profit and crisis: how the system we live in works, seen from below.
luta-pela-terra: The agrarian question, land reform and Brazil's peasant movements.
movimento-estudantil: Student unions, occupations and the defence of public education.
antropologia: Culture, kinship, ritual and difference: the study of ways of living.
servico-social: The social question, public policy and the work of those who serve the people.
arquitetura: The house, the street and the city: how space is built, and for whom.
arquivologia: Keeping, organising and opening up memory: library science, archival science and museology.
dependencia: Why Latin America stays poor even when it grows: Marini, Bambirra, Theotonio dos Santos and the super-exploitation of labour.
imperialismo: Who runs the world and how: finance capital, wars, sanctions, debt and the rivalry between powers today.
ecossocialismo: The climate crisis as a crisis of capitalism: nature, labour and the way out that does not fit into profit.
frances: French from scratch: everyday communication, reading and the French-speaking world.
ingles-infantil: First steps in English for children: everyday words, songs and games.
redes-e-seguranca: How networks work from the inside and how to protect systems and people, with an emphasis on ethical hacking: always authorized and within the law.
trancista: Afro braids: hair care, techniques, history and how to turn the craft into income.
costureira: Sewing from the basics to mending and making garments, and crochet from the first stitch to pieces to sell, with safety at work and ways to earn an income.
engenharia-de-sistemas: How software systems work inside and how to design them to be efficient, reliable and scalable: from the processor to distributed systems.
estado: What is the State and how does it work?
Basic politics for people who never had a politics class: what the State is, who rules, where the money comes from and why it matters to the people.
instituicoes: Congress, Supreme Court, Prosecutor's Office: the institutions
How Congress, the Supreme Court, the Prosecutor General's Office, ministries and city halls work, and how the people press each of them.
eleicoes: How people vote and how votes are counted, what a party is, who funds campaigns and how to watch over those elected.
neurodiversidade: Autism, ADHD, dyslexia and other ways of being and learning, without pathologising, plus an introduction to psychoanalysis.
barbeiro: Men's haircuts and beards: tools, hygiene and biosafety, techniques and how to set up your own work.
oratoria-e-lideranca: Speaking in public with clarity, preparing a talk, running meetings and assemblies and leading collectively.
samba-e-cultura: Samba from the circle to the avenue: history, rhythm, Black and Brazilian culture, the hillside, malandragem and the people who made samba.
eletricista: Electricity from the basics to wiring a house, with safety first: multimeter, breaker panel, outlets, electric shower and the trade as a living.
fotografia: Light, composition and technique to shoot with your phone, document struggles and protect the people in the picture.
web-design: HTML, CSS and accessibility to build light, free websites published at no cost.
alemao: From scratch to reading the news and Brecht in the original, without paying for a course.
ciencias-sociais: Sociology, anthropology and political science together, with methods for doing research alongside the community.
ciencia-politica: State, power, parties and movements, from classical and Marxist theory to imperialism in Latin America.
formacao-militante: Revolutionary theory and organizing practice for those who want to grow as agents of the struggle.

dedication.title: For Lúcia
dedication.etym: From Latin Lucia, feminine of Lucius, derived from lux, lucis: “light”.
senses: The luminous one; she who brings light.
According to tradition, a name given in ancient Rome to children born at dawn.
In this project: the grandmother to whom this library is dedicated.
dedication.related: From the same root: lucid, elucidate, illuminate.
text: This project bears the name of Lúcia, the grandmother of the person who created it.
She is no longer here, but the name remained, and with it what such a name promises: light.
Every library is a way of turning on the light for someone. May everyone who learns something here carry a little of that brightness forward.

punnett.explainMono: Each parent passes on one allele of each gene, at random (Mendel's first law). Every box in the square has the same chance: the phenotype ratio is the chance of each child being born with that trait.
punnett.explainDi: With two genes on different chromosomes, the alleles separate independently (Mendel's second law): that is why a dihybrid cross has 16 boxes and, between two heterozygotes, the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
punnett.explainX: In X-linked inheritance, males have only one X: a single recessive allele is enough for the trait to show. That is why colour blindness and haemophilia are more common in men.

steps: Make sure the place is safe for you. Call the person loudly and tap their shoulders.
If they do not respond and are not breathing normally (or are only gasping), call the emergency number and put it on speaker. Ask someone to look for a defibrillator (AED) nearby.
Kneel beside them. Put the heel of one hand in the centre of the chest and the other hand on top, arms straight.
Push hard and fast: 5 to 6 cm deep in an adult, 100 to 120 times a minute, to the rhythm of this beat.
Let the chest come all the way back up between compressions. Do not stop: if someone else is there, swap every 2 minutes, quickly.
Keep going until the ambulance team arrives or the person starts breathing again. If an AED arrives, switch it on and follow its instructions.
cpr.warning: This does not replace a first aid course. The technique is different for children and babies.

surplus.explain: In Marx's account, the working day has two parts. During necessary labour, the worker produces the equivalent of their own wage (variable capital, v). During surplus labour, they keep producing, but that value, the surplus value (s), goes to whoever owns the means of production. The rate s/v, equal to surplus labour ÷ necessary labour, measures the degree of exploitation.

support.title: Support Instituto Lúcia
support.lead: The library is free and has no ads, and it will stay that way, with or without your contribution.
paragraphs: Instituto Lúcia has no sponsor, sells no courses and does not sell your data. It is kept going by volunteer work, because knowledge is not a commodity.

Even so, keeping a site online costs money. Those who can help pay that bill guarantee access for those who cannot. That is how the working class has always built what is its own: by pooling the little each one has.
The money raised has a clear destination:
costs: Domain and hosting for the site.
Storage for audio and for backup copies of the collection.
Whatever is left goes into expanding the collection: more lessons, more translations, more reviewing.

povo.title: People's data
povo.lead: The numbers that weigh most on working people's lives, and what the Chamber of Deputies is voting, straight from official Brazilian sources. Updated every few hours.

salario: Monthly value of the national minimum wage (Brazil).
ipca: IPCA accumulated over twelve months: how much prices rose in a year.
selic: Annual Selic target set by the Central Bank. It makes credit dearer or cheaper.
desocupacao: Unemployment rate from the PNAD Contínua survey, rolling quarter.
rendimento: Average monthly income of working people, adjusted for inflation (Continuous PNAD, rolling quarter).
informalidade: Share of workers without a formal contract or registration, and so without rights such as paid leave and a pension.
dolar: Commercial dollar selling rate. When it rises, so do bread, gas and fuel prices.
rotativo: Average yearly rate for people who pay only part of their card bill. It is the most expensive credit in the country.
endividamento: How much families owe banks, compared with a full year of income.
comprometimento: Share of families’ monthly income that goes to interest and instalments owed to banks.
inadimplencia: Share of personal credit more than 90 days overdue (non-earmarked loans).

zinePassos: Print on an A4 sheet lying down (landscape), with the smallest possible margin.
Fold the sheet in half lengthwise and open it. Fold it in half widthwise, in half again, and open it.
Fold it in half widthwise and cut only the middle crease, between the two central panels.
Open it, fold it lengthwise and push the ends towards the centre: the panels become an 8-page booklet, with the cover on the outside.

guia: The facilitator doesn't need to be a teacher or know everything. The job is to open the conversation, keep time and make sure everyone gets to speak.
Before: read the lesson, choose the opening question and check that the place is accessible and safe. Starting on time and having water helps a lot.
Agreements to read at the start: everyone speaks and nobody interrupts; nobody has to read aloud; there are no silly questions here; what is said in the nucleus stays in the nucleus.
During: ask more than you explain. When someone brings a case from their own life, connect it to the lesson. If the conversation stalls, go back to the discussion questions.

Safety: don't photograph or film anyone who doesn't want it; don't post participants' addresses, names or faces on open networks; to spread the word, use the poster with the nucleus contact, never a person's.
If harassment or threats happen, stop the activity, support whoever was affected and tell the institute through the Report page.
Afterwards: write one line on what worked and what to change. If you want, register the nucleus with the institute team, who send materials and support.

eixos.title: The 12 axes test
eixos.description: Find out where you stand on 12 political axes, from economics to social values, and which ideologies are closest to your ideas.
eixos.lead: Say how much you agree with each statement. At the end you see where you stand on each of the 12 axes and the three ideologies closest to your answers. There are no right answers: the test is for thinking and studying, not for labelling anyone.

eixos.closest: The ideologies closest to your answers
eixos.methodText: Each statement pulls one axis toward one side. Strongly agreeing counts a full point toward the statement's side, agreeing counts half a point, disagreeing pulls toward the other side and neutral doesn't pull. The percentage shows where your answers went on each axis. Ideologies are compared by the distance between your twelve numbers and each one's typical position, which is an approximation: every current has many variations.
